title: Mirror & Water Images
summary: A vertical mirror reverses left-right (character order reversed and every character flipped); water reverses top-bottom (order kept, characters upside down). Know the symmetric letters for each (AHIMOTUVWXY for mirrors, BCDEHIKOX for water), use 11:60 − time for clock mirrors, and track one asymmetric feature in figure questions.

subtopics.title: Mirror images (vertical mirror)
subtopics.concept: A vertical mirror swaps left and right and keeps top and bottom. In a word or number, the order of the characters is reversed, and every character is flipped left to right. Letters with a vertical line of symmetry look unchanged. Use them as quick check points.

tricks.title: Check the ends first
tricks.body: The image starts with the last character of the word, flipped. Reject options by looking at the first character only.

example.q: What does the mirror image of PEN7 start with?
steps: The last character is 7.
It comes first in the image and faces the other way.

tricks.title: Symmetric-letter shortcut
tricks.body: A word made only of A H I M O T U V W X Y that reads the same backwards looks unchanged in a vertical mirror.

example.q: Does MOM look the same in a vertical mirror?
steps: M and O are symmetric.
MOM reads the same backwards.

mistakes.wrong: Flipping each letter but keeping the original order.
mistakes.right: Reverse the order first. The last character comes first.

mistakes.wrong: Reversing the order but not flipping the letters.
mistakes.right: Flip every asymmetric letter left to right as well.

mistakes.wrong: Turning letters upside down in a mirror image.
mistakes.right: A vertical mirror keeps top and bottom. Upside down is a water image.

mistakes.wrong: Saying a palindrome always looks the same in a mirror.
mistakes.right: Every letter must also be symmetric. NOON reads the same backwards, but N is not symmetric.

mistakes.wrong: Using the mirror list of letters for a water image.
mistakes.right: Water has its own list: B C D E H I K O X.

subtopics.notes:
### What a vertical mirror does
Stand in front of a mirror and raise your right hand. The image raises the hand on the other side.

A vertical mirror swaps left and right. Top stays top. It does not matter if the mirror is on the left or the right of the object. The image looks the same.

For a word, number or code, two things happen together:

1. The order is reversed. The last character comes first.
2. Each character is flipped left to right. R, E, S, N, 2, 4 and 7 face the other way.

> **Rule:** Mirror image = reverse the order + flip every character. Top stays top.

### Letters that look the same
Capitals with a vertical line of symmetry look the same in a mirror.

**A H I M O T U V W X Y**, and the digits 0 and 8.

All other capitals look reversed: B C D E F G J K L N P Q R S Z.

A whole word looks the same in a mirror only if two things are true:

- it reads the same backwards, and
- every letter is in the list above.

Examples: MOM, WOW, TOOT, MAAM.

### Four-step check for options
1. The first character of the image is the last character of the word. Reject options that start with anything else.
2. Check one asymmetric character, such as R, E, S, 4 or 7. It must face the other way.
3. Check that top stays top. An upside-down letter means a water image or a half turn.
4. Check the middle characters only if two options are left.

> **Tip:** Two checks, the first character and one flipped letter, often leave only one option.

### The usual wrong options
- Water image: order kept, letters upside down.
- Half turn: order reversed and letters upside down. It is a mirror image plus a water image.
- Reversed only: order reversed, but letters not flipped.
- Flipped only: letters flipped, but order kept.

### Figures
In a line figure, every point moves to the same distance on the other side of the mirror line. Left goes to right. Height does not change.

Pick one clear feature: a dot, a shaded corner or a short tail. Check where it lands.

- Top-left goes to top-right in a mirror image.
- Bottom-left would be a water image.
- Bottom-right would be a half turn.

### Place in the image
Some questions ask which letter is at a given place, counting from the left, in the mirror image.

Write the word backwards. Then count from the left in the new order.

Example: the mirror image of PLANET reads T, E, N, A, L, P. The 3rd letter from the left is N.

> **Note:** A mirror on the left or on the right gives the same image. Only its position changes.

### Worked example
Mirror image of REASON.

The image reads N O S A E R from left to right. A and O are symmetric, so they look the same. N, S, E and R face the other way.

An option showing N O S A E R with upside-down letters is a half turn, not a mirror image.

subtopics.title: Water images (horizontal mirror)
subtopics.concept: Water below an object works as a horizontal mirror. It swaps top and bottom and keeps left and right. In a water image the order of the characters stays the same, and every character is turned upside down. Letters with a horizontal line of symmetry look unchanged.

tricks.title: Order stays, letters go upside down
tricks.body: In the options, look for the one that keeps the original order and has only the unsymmetric letters turned upside down.

example.q: What is the water image of BOX?
steps: B, O and X are all symmetric top to bottom.
Water keeps the order.

tricks.title: Name the image from two clues
tricks.body: Same order and upside down: water. Reversed order and flipped left to right: mirror. Reversed and upside down: half turn.

example.q: A word appears with its order reversed and every letter upside down. What is this image?
steps: The order is reversed, so it is not water.
Letters are also upside down, so it is not a mirror image.

mistakes.wrong: Reversing the order of the characters in a water image.
mistakes.right: Water keeps the order. Only top and bottom swap.

mistakes.wrong: Spinning letters through a half turn instead of flipping them top to bottom.
mistakes.right: A water image is a flip. Left-facing parts still face left.

mistakes.wrong: Using the mirror list A H I M O T U V W X Y for water.
mistakes.right: Water list: B C D E H I K O X.

mistakes.wrong: Thinking 6 upside down becomes 9 in water.
mistakes.right: 9 is a half turn of 6. A water image flips top to bottom only.

mistakes.wrong: Calling a reversed, upside-down word a mirror image.
mistakes.right: Reversed order plus upside down is a half turn.

subtopics.notes:
### What water does
A lake below a hill shows the hill upside down. The water surface is a horizontal mirror below the object.

It swaps top and bottom. It keeps left and right. A question may say "the mirror is placed horizontally below" or "along line MN below the figure". All of these mean a water image.

For a word, number or code:

1. The order stays the same. The first character is still first.
2. Each character is flipped top to bottom.

> **Rule:** Water image = keep the order + flip every character top to bottom.

### Letters that look the same
Capitals with a horizontal line of symmetry look the same in water.

**B C D E H I K O X**, and the digits 0, 3 and 8.

A word looks the same in water if every letter is in this list. It does not need to be a palindrome, because water keeps the order.

Examples: CHOICE, BOX, HIDE, CODE, DECIDE.

> **Watch:** A, M, T, U, V, W and Y are symmetric in a mirror but not in water. M upside down looks like W.

### Four-step check for options
1. The first character stays first. An option that starts with the last character is a mirror image or a half turn.
2. Check one letter that is not in the list, such as A, R, T, 4 or 7. It must be upside down.
3. Parts that faced left must still face left. The bowl of R stays on the right side.
4. Compare the rest only if two options are left.

### Mirror plus water is a half turn
A mirror image followed by a water image, in either order, is a half turn (180 degrees). The order is reversed and every character is upside down.

After a half turn, H, I, N, O, S, X, Z, 0 and 8 look unchanged. So SOS, NOON and XOX look the same after a half turn.

### Figures
Every point moves to the same distance on the other side of the horizontal line. Top goes to bottom. Left and right do not change.

- Top-left goes to bottom-left in a water image.
- Top-right would be a mirror image.
- Bottom-right would be a half turn.

> **Tip:** Track one feature, such as a shaded corner. It tells you the image type at once.

### Naming the image
Look at two things: is the order reversed, and is anything upside down?

| Order | Letters | Image |
|---|---|---|
| Reversed | Flipped left to right | Mirror image |
| Same | Upside down | Water image |
| Reversed | Upside down | Half turn |

### Numbers in water
Digits follow the same rule. Keep the order and flip each digit top to bottom.

0, 3 and 8 look unchanged. In 83602, the digits 8, 3 and 0 look the same, while 6 and 2 look different.

### Worked example
Water image of BUDGET.

The order stays B U D G E T. B, D and E look unchanged. U, G and T appear upside down. An option that begins with T is not a water image.

subtopics.title: Mirror image of a clock
subtopics.concept: A clock seen in a vertical mirror has its hands swapped across the 12-6 line. The actual time and the image time always add up to 12:00. So image time = 11:60 minus actual time, and the same rule works both ways.

formulas.name: Mirror time
formulas.note: Works in both directions. For 12:xx, use 23:60 minus the time.

tricks.title: 11:60 rule
tricks.body: Subtract the hours from 11 and the minutes from 60.

example.q: A clock shows 4:20. What does its mirror image show?

tricks.title: Check by adding
tricks.body: Add the given time and your answer. The sum must be 12:00.

example.q: The mirror image of a clock shows 5:35. Is 6:25 the actual time?

mistakes.wrong: Subtracting from 12:00 and slipping on the borrow.
Using the rule on 12:xx times without adding 12 first.
Mirroring the hours and keeping the minutes.
mistakes.right: Both hands swap. Subtract the whole time from 11:60.

mistakes.wrong: Adding the elapsed time to the mirror reading.
mistakes.right: Find the actual time first. Then add the elapsed time.

mistakes.wrong: Picking the half-turn time as the mirror time.
mistakes.right: The half-turn time is the actual time plus 6 hours. The mirror time adds up to 12:00.

subtopics.notes:
### Why the 11:60 rule works
A clock in a vertical mirror has its hands swapped across the line from 12 to 6. A hand 20 minutes past 12 on the right shows 20 minutes before 12 on the left.

So the actual time and the image time always add up to 12:00.

$$\text{image} = 11{:}60 - \text{actual}$$

Writing 12:00 as 11:60 saves you from borrowing. The rule works both ways: actual $= 11{:}60 -$ image.

Examples:
- $3{:}45$ gives $11{:}60 - 3{:}45 = 8{:}15$
- $10{:}10$ gives $1{:}50$
- $7{:}05$ gives $4{:}55$

> **Rule:** Actual time + image time = 12:00.

### Special times
- 12:00 and 6:00 look the same in a mirror. These are the only two such times. Both hands then lie on the 12-6 line.
- Times from 12:00 to 12:59: use $23{:}60 -$ time. So 12:20 gives 11:40.
- Whole hours: $h{:}00$ gives $(12-h){:}00$. So 4:00 gives 8:00.
- With seconds: use $11{:}59{:}60 -$ time. So 2:25:40 gives 9:34:20.

### Reading a clock face
Sometimes a figure shows a mirrored clock with no numbers.

1. The 12 mark is still at the top.
2. Read the time the hands seem to show. That is the image time.
3. Actual time $= 11{:}60 -$ image time.

A hand pointing to the 2 position in the image was really pointing to the 10 position.

### Why the hour drops by one
Take 3:45. The hour hand is three-quarters of the way from 3 to 4. In the mirror it is three-quarters of the way from 9 to 8. It is past 8, not past 9.

So the image shows 8:15, not 9:15. When the minutes are not zero, the image hour is $11 - h$, not $12 - h$.

> **Watch:** Doing $12 - 3 = 9$ and $60 - 45 = 15$ gives 9:15. That is wrong.

### Two-step questions
The mirror shows 4:20. What is the actual time after 1 hour 15 minutes?

First find the actual time: $11{:}60 - 4{:}20 = 7{:}40$. Then add: $7{:}40 + 1{:}15 = 8{:}55$.

Convert first, then add. A mirror of a mirror gives back the actual time.

### Wrong options to expect
- Half-turn time: $3{:}45 + 6{:}00 = 9{:}45$ is where the hands are after a half turn. It is not the mirror image.
- Hours mirrored, minutes kept: 8:45 is only half the job.
- Borrowing slip: subtracting the hours from 12 instead of 11.

### Water image of a clock
A water image swaps top and bottom of the clock face. The hands then point to places that no real time gives.

So exams ask about mirror images of clocks. If a question shows a water image, the clock face is turned upside down, and you read it that way.

### Worked example
The mirror image of a clock shows 5:35. Find the actual time.

Actual $= 11{:}60 - 5{:}35 = 6{:}25$.

Check: $5{:}35 + 6{:}25 = 12{:}00$. An option of 7:25 forgets to borrow. 11:35 is the half-turn time.

> **Tip:** Always add your answer to the given time. The sum must be exactly 12:00.

practice.q: A wall clock shows **3:45**. What time will its mirror image show?
A wall clock shows **10:10**. What time will its mirror image show?
A wall clock shows **6:35**. What time will its mirror image show?
Seen in a mirror, a clock appears to show **2:25**. What is the actual time?
practice.solution: The rule works both ways: actual = 11:60 − 2:25 = **9:35**. Check: mirror of 9:35 = 11:60 − 9:35 = 2:25.
practice.shortcut: Same 11:60 rule in reverse.

practice.q: A clock shows **12:20**. What time does its mirror image show?
practice.solution: For 12:xx times use 23:60: 23:60 − 12:20 = 11:40. Check: 12:20 + 11:40 = 24:00, i.e. the hands mirror across the 12–6 line → **11:40**.
practice.shortcut: 12:xx → subtract from 23:60.

options: DEED
BOB
WOW
NOON
practice.solution: A word looks unchanged in a vertical mirror only if (i) it reads the same backwards and (ii) every letter is left-right symmetric (A H I M O T U V W X Y). All four are palindromes, but N, D and B are not left-right symmetric. Only **WOW** passes both tests.
practice.shortcut: Palindrome + only AHIMOTUVWXY letters.

practice.q: Which of the following words will look **exactly the same** in its water image?
options: BRIDGE
CHANCE
EXPECT
CHOICE
practice.solution: Water keeps the order, so a word is unchanged only if every letter is top-bottom symmetric (B C D E H I K O X). CHOICE = C, H, O, I, C, E — all symmetric. BRIDGE has R and G, CHANCE has A and N, EXPECT has P and T. Answer: **CHOICE**.
practice.shortcut: Every letter must be in BCDEHIKOX.

practice.q: How many letters of the word **BACKGROUND** look exactly the same in a water image (considered one by one)?
practice.solution: Top-bottom symmetric capitals: B C D E H I K O X. Letter by letter in B A C K G R O U N D: B ✓, A ✗, C ✓, K ✓, G ✗, R ✗, O ✓, U ✗, N ✗, D ✓ → **5**.
practice.shortcut: Tick letters from BCDEHIKOX.

practice.q: How many letters of the word **AUTOMOBILE** look exactly the same in a vertical mirror (checked one by one)?
practice.solution: Letters that look the same in a vertical mirror: A H I M O T U V W X Y. In A U T O M O B I L E, the matching letters are A, U, T, O, M, O, I = **7**. The rest (B, L, E) change.
practice.shortcut: Tick letters from A H I M O T U V W X Y; count repeats.

practice.q: Which word will look **exactly the same** in a vertical mirror?
options: TOOK
NOON
TOOT
DEED
practice.solution: In a mirror a word looks unchanged only if it reads the same backwards **and** every letter is in A H I M O T U V W X Y. **TOOT** passes both tests. NOON has N, which is not symmetric; DEED has D, E, which are not symmetric; TOOK does not read the same backwards.

practice.q: Which word will look **exactly the same** in its water image?
options: FIXED
BOXER
BOXED
MIXED
practice.solution: Water keeps the order, so a word looks unchanged if every letter is in B C D E H I K O X. **BOXED** uses only these letters. BOXER has R; MIXED has M; FIXED has F.

practice.q: A word is seen in a vertical mirror, and that image is then seen in water. Which word will look **exactly the same** at the end?
options: SOS
NUN
DAD
TOT
practice.solution: A mirror image followed by a water image is a 180° turn: the order is reversed and each letter is turned upside down. The word looks unchanged only if it reads the same backwards and every letter is in H I N O S X Z. **SOS** passes. DAD has D, A, which change in a half turn; TOT has T, which changes in a half turn; NUN has U, which changes in a half turn.

practice.q: A wall clock shows **4:40**. What time will its mirror image show?
practice.solution: Actual time + image time = 12:00, so the answer is 11:60 − 4:40 = **7:20**. Check: 4:40 + 7:20 = 12:00.
practice.shortcut: Subtract from 11:60.

practice.q: A wall clock shows **2:25:40**. What time will its mirror image show?
practice.solution: Actual time + image time = 12:00, so the answer is 11:59:60 − 2:25:40 = **9:34:20**. Check: 2:25:40 + 9:34:20 = 12:00. With seconds, write 12:00:00 as 11:59:60.
practice.shortcut: Subtract from 11:59:60.

practice.q: At which of these times will a clock and its mirror image show **the same time**?
practice.solution: The image equals the actual time only when both hands lie on the 12–6 line, because only that line is its own mirror image. That happens at 12:00 and **6:00**. At 3:00 the image shows 9:00; at 9:30 it shows 2:30; at 12:30 it shows 11:30.
practice.shortcut: Only 12:00 and 6:00 are unchanged.

practice.q: A clock seen in a mirror shows **4:20**. What will the **actual** time be 1 hour 15 minutes later?
practice.solution: First convert the mirror reading: actual = 11:60 − 4:20 = 7:40. Then add 1 hour 15 minutes: **8:55**. Adding first and converting afterwards gives 6:25, which is wrong because time passes on the real clock.
practice.shortcut: Convert to the actual time first, then add or subtract.
